source.extractionNote: Both variants read in full; intent from the Screen Header Bar Metadata frame via the 2026-11-04 spec.

summary: The bar at the top of a screen, carrying a back affordance, the screen's title and one action. It holds a single slot on the right, so it suits a screen with exactly one primary action rather than a toolbar of several. Use Top App Bar when the screen needs more than one action or a different leading control.

intent.text: The screen's name, and the thing a reader orients by. Name the screen rather than the task in progress, because the bar does not change as someone works and a title implying progress goes stale the moment they act.

intent.true: Show the back affordance. Leave it on for any screen pushed on top of another, which is the case this bar is drawn for.
intent.false: Drop it on a root screen with nowhere to go back to. The heading takes the reclaimed space, so nothing else needs adjusting.

intent.true: Despite the name this does not round the bar. It sets the contour of the action button in the slot, so pick the value matching the buttons used elsewhere on the screen.
intent.false: The sharp pairing for that same button. It reaches only the button shipped in the slot, so replacing the slot content drops the connection entirely.

rounded.note: Since the Oct 7, 2026 file change it also sets the leading Icon Button's shape; the metadata still says slot-button only (see issues).

actionSlot.default: one primary Button (Size=medium, Shape per rounded, label "Button")

intent.slot: Holds the trailing action and hugs whatever is placed in it. It ships a Button at Size=medium and Flavour=primary. Nothing limits it to one control, so a crowded slot is possible and is the thing to watch.

internalVariations.pinned: Size=medium, Flavour=subtle, State=default, Disabled=false; Shape follows rounded; glyph chevron-left (rounded family, Icon Size=medium)
internalVariations.intent: An Icon at Size=medium swapped to Chevron Left. Only its visibility is surfaced, so the glyph cannot be changed from an instance without detaching.
internalVariations.decision: The instance (and its Icon) is actually exposed, so the glyph and button props are editable per instance, contradicting the metadata. Whether they become props in code is the implementer's call.

anatomy.role: The bar itself. Transparent fill, no border, no shadow, no radius; the width is fixed rather than filling.
The back chevron, present when Show Leading Icon is on. A locked Icon instance with only its visibility exposed.
The title wrapper. It fills the space between the icon and the slot, which is what holds the action hard right.
The trailing region a consumer fills. It hugs its content, so the heading absorbs whatever width is left.

variants._note: Nothing else differs between the two variants.

states.change: The set declares no hover, focus, pressed or disabled axis. The two variants render identically apart from the corners of the action button.
The back affordance is removed and the heading absorbs the 28px it occupied. Nothing else moves, because the bar's width is fixed.

behavior.description: Figma stores no timing and no transition is authored. Nothing in the set changes over time.
The leading chevron is a locked Icon instance with no state of its own. What it does on activation, and whether it is reachable at all, belongs to the implementation.
Rounded is a variant on this set rather than a property passed down, so it restyles the shipped action button and nothing else. Slot content put there later will not follow it.

content.description: Plain text set per instance, defaulting to Add Subscribers. The heading wrapper is built with a gap for a second line, but no subtitle property exists to fill it.

Holds the trailing action and hugs whatever is placed in it. It ships a Button at Size=medium and Flavour=primary. Nothing limits it to one control, so a crowded slot is possible and is the thing to watch.

content.type: fixed nested Icon, toggled by Show Leading Icon
content.description: An Icon at Size=medium swapped to Chevron Left. Only its visibility is surfaced, so the glyph cannot be changed from an instance without detaching.

do: Use it as the top bar of a pushed screen, with the back chevron on and a single action on the right.
Match Rounded to the buttons used elsewhere on the screen. It exists to keep the action button consistent, not to shape the bar.
dont: Don't put more than one control in the Action Slot. It will hug them, but the bar was drawn around a single action.
Don't assume the bar stretches to the screen. It ships at a fixed width, so it has to be set to fill wherever it is placed.

accessibility: The leading chevron is a locked icon with no label and no state. It needs an accessible name and a keyboard path, neither of which is modelled here.
No focus state exists anywhere in the set, so focus order and a visible focus ring both have to come from code.
The title uses title/large. It names the screen, so it should map to a real heading in the markup rather than being styled text.
The bar's fill is interactive/ghost/background/default, an interactive token on a static container. Check it against the screen behind it and against the action button sitting on it.
Turning the leading icon off removes the only back affordance. On a pushed screen something else then has to provide one.

layoutTheming.description: 474 wide and 56 tall in both variants. The width is fixed rather than filling, so a placed instance will not stretch to its container on its own.
space/sm top and bottom, space/lg left and right, with a space/sm gap between the icon, the heading and the slot.
Horizontal auto-layout, items centred on the cross axis and packed from the start. The heading fills, which pushes the slot hard right.
Zero on both variants with no token bound. The Rounded axis does not touch it.
interactive/ghost/background/default, an interactive token on a static container. No border and no shadow.
title/large, in foreground/primary. This style resolves to a remote library rather than a local one.
Icon at Size=medium, 20 square. Hiding it returns 28px to the heading, the icon plus one gap.

issues.detail: Rounded reach: since the Oct 7 change, rounded also sets the leading Icon Button (rounded with radius/element-sm, or sharp with radius/none). The metadata still says it reaches only the slot button, under Property Breakdown and Behavior & Motion Intent.
Heading padding: Heading Content binds space/gutter left and right, spacing the title from the back button and the action. Layout & Theming does not mention it.

Leading icon: the metadata calls it a locked Icon at Size=medium, 20 square, with no state. It is actually an Icon Button (medium, subtle, shape per rounded) sized control/md with space/2xs padding, wrapping that Icon — a control with its own state axis, about twice the size the metadata states.
Exposed instance: the metadata says only visibility is surfaced. Leading Icon is an exposed nested instance and its Icon is exposed too, so the glyph and button props are editable per instance.
Size: the metadata says 56 tall. Measured height is 64Px (space/md top and bottom around control/md controls). Width matches.
Padding & gap: the metadata says space/sm top/bottom, space/lg left/right, space/sm gap. Bound: top/right/bottom space/md, left space/sm, gap space/2xs. space/lg is unused.
Reclaimed width: the metadata says hiding the icon returns 28px. It returns control/md plus the space/2xs gap.

Remote variables: the root fill, foreground/primary, space/2xs on the heading, space/xs on the title row, and all five title/large/* font variables are bound to remote library copies of same-named variables. Every name resolves in tokens/, so code is unaffected. The Figma file should be relinked to its local variables.
The metadata says the title style resolves to a remote library. The title/large text style is local; only the variables bound on the title node are remote.
The root fill (and the Icon Button's fill override) has paint opacity zero, so the bar is transparent whatever interactive/ghost/background/default resolves to.
Action Slot is missing from the Property Breakdown table; it appears only under Content & Slot. The other defaults match Figma.
The slot is a native SLOT property with Button and Icon Button as preferred values. Preferred-only is off and it has no min/max, so one action is guidance only.
The heading wrapper (space/2xs) and title row (space/xs) have gaps but only a single child each; no subtitle property exists.
The root width is fixed (474Px measured). Usage says to set it to fill; implement it as the full width of its container.

The set has no description. No interactive states or motion exist, by design. The back button's activation and accessible name are left to code. It overlaps Top App Bar, which covers the same role with more layouts.
